instruction.text: Which agricultural problems arise in a modern world? Complete the sentences.

atoms.a: Chemical pesticides are used to kill harmful insects and weeds,
atoms.b: but they also harm insects and plants that do not negatively impact the crops.

atoms.a: Many low-income countries do not have the resources to feed their whole population,
atoms.b: which leads to diseases and nutrient deficiencies.

atoms.a: Climate change causes great changes in temperature and rainfall,
atoms.b: often causing crops to fail due to heatwaves and droughts.

instruction.text: Read the text. Which positive aspect of gene-modified crops does golden rice represent?

atoms.text: Golden rice has been genetically modified to produce more beta-carotene, a substance that the human body converts into vitamin A. It was developed to be grown in low-income countries to combat famine.

b: ++It is more nutritious than regular rice.
It is more resistant to climate change.
The plants produce a larger amount of rice.

instruction.text: Which negative consequences could arise from this? Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Native varieties of rice could die out, leading to less ((++biodiversity)).
Local ((farmers)) could become dependent on corporations ((distributing)) this type of rice.
The genes could have unwanted ((effects)) on humans, such as causing ((allergies)).

instruction.text: Read and answer the questions below. Multiple answers may be correct.

atoms.text: Bt cotton has been inserted with a gene from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis to produce a toxin which specifically targets the bollworm, a moth larva that mainly eats cotton plants.

atoms.a: Which positive aspect of gene-modified crops does Bt cotton represent?
b: It grows faster than regular cotton.
It requires less water than usual.

atoms.a: Why is that a good thing?
b: ++If the plant produces its own pesticide, less chemical pesticides have to be used.
++The pesticide targets only one specific species, meaning that non-harmful bugs can thrive.
Pesticides make the plants safer to eat for humans.

atoms.text: Bt cotton now makes up over 90% of all cotton grown in India. However, in many areas, bollworms have developed an immunity to the toxin. Farmers complain that even additional chemical pesticides do not kill the insects anymore. In the long run, this means GM crops have only made the original problem worse.

instruction.text: Choose whether the statements are true or false.

atoms.a: In some places, the bugs targeted by the pesticide have become unaffected by it.
Bollworms now pose a bigger problem than before the introduction of Bt cotton.
Spraying the plants with chemical pesticides helps combat the issue.
